review_text_raw:
While I think this a good game and definitely worth checking out, I do want to say that I haven't finished the game and may not. The story was interesting and when it progressed it was always the highlight of the experience, but the base gameplay just got to me in the end. It's hard for me not to compare it to Orwell, which is better experience for a similar story.

While you are a government agent doing hacking research and discovering enemies of the state, most of the game you lose information between cases and the clues aren't always intuitive. And it didn't help that the UI is worse than Windows 3.1. A lot of the times it just felt like playing the game was harder than it needed to be with no good reason. Like, if I download a document and realize I don't need it, why can't I place it in the trash bin to get it out of the way. Even in a similar desktop manager like Paper's, Please, you could move junk out of your way. And it doesn't help to keep me immersed as an agent with all this tech to spy on people, but I can't delete a picture I mistakenly downloaded.

I would highly suggest trying out the demo first. I think you get a good intro to how the game works by then. If you like it, pick it up, but I personally would wait for a sale.

review_text_raw:
It's a "short" PnC adventure. It's fun and interesting until you get stuck trying to figure out what the right evidence combinations are supposed to be because it's not clear what really counts as evidence. It also doesn't support expected keyboard features, like copy/paste and highlighting, so it's tedious to type out IP addresses and there's too many opportunities to screw it up. 

I personally had fun playing this, but would I really recommend this for someone else? Not really.

review_text_raw:
This game is short but sweet, very very sweet, it had a feel similar to Orwell except for the fact that it doesn't highlight clues for you, it was both challenging and easy to grasp and get into and not want to leave. I did find the story overall pretty good and I can't wait to see future projects from these developers. 
The one downside for this game is replay value where it sits with little to none, but for me that is not too bad.
In summary if you like espionage/ surveillance games (such as Orwell, Don't Feed The Monkeys, etc.,) what are you waiting for this game is Awesome!!
